cse-1997-a-34.approach: With one accumulator, the running value $(a*b)*c$ can stay in the register only if it is the left operand of the next operation that is performed; that holds for left-associative operators of equal or lower precedence (+, *), but not for ↑.

steps.title: Accumulator evaluation
steps.body: LOAD a; MUL b; MUL c leaves $(a*b)*c$ in the register. Next the machine can only do `OP operand` with the register as left operand.

steps.title: op = + or *
steps.body: `+` has lower precedence and `*` is left-associative, so $(a*b)*c\ \text{op}\ d$ is evaluated as $((a*b)*c)\ \text{op}\ d$: just `ADD d` / `MUL d` — no store needed.

steps.title: op = ↑
steps.body: ↑ binds tighter than *, so the expression is $(a*b)*(c\uparrow d)$: $c\uparrow d$ must be computed first in the only register, so $(a*b)$ has to be saved. Hence (A).

optionAnalysis.reason: Correct: for + and * the accumulated value is the left operand of the next operation.
↑ has higher precedence than *, forcing $c\uparrow\ldots$ first and a store of $(a*b)$.
Same problem with ↑.
